# The projective-energy maximal stratum of actual deepest points

This note proves a rigid maximum stratum for an arbitrary actual finite
family of positive, parallel, full-dimensional convex fibers. It does
not assume a shape-minimizing family, critical-cap regularity, or a free
deformation. It proves no descent and does not classify all deepest
fibers.

The new input is the jointly concave energy and its complete equality
classification in
`candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56`,
independently audited in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. Actual geometry and the precise deepest set

Let `d>=1` and let `P=conv(P) intersect Z^n` be finite and nonempty.
For each `p in P`, let `K_p` be a compact convex body in `R^d`. Assume
every anchored convex representation satisfies the actual inclusion

    q=sum_i lambda_i p_i in P  =>
    sum_i lambda_i K_(p_i) subset K_q.                 (1)

Use the actual mixed measure
`mu=sum_(p in P) delta_p tensor Lebesgue_d|K_p` and its raw ambient
halfspace depth `D_mu(Y)`, defined using closed containing halfspaces.
Write

    S=union_(p in P) {p} times K_p,
    Q=max_(Y in S) D_mu(Y)>0,
    D={Y in R^(n+d):D_mu(Y)>=Q}.                        (2)

The set `D` is the REAL depth superlevel set. Its points at noninteger
bases may have depth strictly greater than `Q`; only `D intersect S`
is the actual mixed deepest set. This distinction is retained throughout.

For a fixed unit ambient normal, the closed through-point cap mass is
upper semicontinuous in its source point, by reverse Fatou for the
closed halfspace indicators. The infimum over normals is therefore
upper semicontinuous. Every containing halfspace at a convex combination
contains at least one positively weighted input point. Consequently
depth superlevel sets are convex. Outside the compact convex hull of
`S`, strict separation gives depth zero. Thus `D` is compact and convex,
and `D intersect S` is compact. A point interior to any own fiber has
positive depth supplied by that fiber alone, proving `Q>0` and its
attainment.

All points of `D intersect S` lie in their own fiber interiors. Here is
a finite support proof in the present parallel full-dimensional setting.
At an own-boundary point `y in K_p`, choose a unit supporting normal `u`
with `u.y=h_p(u)`. There exists a base vector `A` such that

    h_z(u)<=h_p(u)+A.(z-p) for every z in P.             (3)

Indeed, finite Farkas infeasibility would supply nonnegative weights
whose base barycenter is `p` and whose weighted supports exceed
`h_p(u)`, contradicting (1). The closed containing ambient halfspace
`u.x>=h_p(u)+A.(z-p)` then has in each fiber only an empty or supporting
trace, of zero `d`-volume. Hence the source depth is zero. This argument
also covers `n=0`; no base vector is then needed.

## 2. A strict inclusion lemma for the energy

For `y in int K`, define

    E_K(y)=min_a int_K [1+a.(x-y)]^(-d-1) dx,           (4)

with the denominator positive on all of `K`. The cited energy theorem
proves positivity, unique attainment, joint Minkowski concavity of
`E^(1/d)`, strict fixed-body concavity, and equality exactly for marked
positive homotheties.

If `K subset L`, `K!=L`, and `y in int K`, then

    E_K(y)<E_L(y).                                      (5)

To see this, use the attained minimizer `a_L` for the larger body.
Proper inclusion of full-dimensional compact convex bodies gives
`|L\K|>0`: a strict separating functional for a point of `L\K`,
together with an interior ball of `K`, exhibits positive volume outside
`K`. The integrand at `a_L` is continuous and strictly positive on `L`.
Therefore

    E_L(y)=int_L L_(a_L)^(-d-1)
           >int_K L_(a_L)^(-d-1)>=E_K(y).

There is no interchange of minimizers or admissible parameter domains.

## 3. Maximum-stratum theorem

Define

    R=max_{(p,y) in D intersect S} E_(K_p)(y)^(1/d),
    J={p in P: some (p,y) in D has E_(K_p)(y)^(1/d)=R}. (6)

Then `R>0` is attained, `J` is nonempty, and the following hold.

1. At each `p in J` there is exactly one such marked point, denoted
   `y_p`.
2. `J=conv(J) intersect Z^n`.
3. For ANY positive-weight representation using points of `J`,

       q=sum_i lambda_i p_i in Z^n,

   its target belongs to `J`, and

       y_q=sum_i lambda_i y_(p_i),
       K_q=sum_i lambda_i K_(p_i),
       K_(p_i)-y_(p_i)=K_q-y_q  for every i.            (7)

In particular every distinct same-parity pair in `J`, together with
its integer midpoint, has identical translated fibers centered at its
selected deepest points and exact midpoint equality.

Proof of attainment: on each fixed fiber interior, `E^(1/d)` is finite
and concave, hence continuous. The compact set `D intersect S` avoids
every own-fiber boundary, and there are finitely many fibers. Its
positive continuous energy therefore attains `R`.

If two different points in one fiber both attained `R`, their midpoint
would belong to `D` by convexity, while strict fixed-body energy
concavity would give a larger energy. This proves uniqueness in part 1.

For the representation in part 3, let `y=sum_i lambda_i y_(p_i)` and
`L=sum_i lambda_i K_(p_i)`. Completeness of `P` gives `q in P`, (1)
gives `L subset K_q`, and the positive input interior balls show
`y in int L`. Convexity of `D` puts `(q,y)` in `D`; since its base is
integer, it is an actual deepest point. Hence the defining maximum and
the joint energy theorem give the full chain

    R >= E_(K_q)(y)^(1/d)
      >= E_L(y)^(1/d)
      >= sum_i lambda_i E_(K_(p_i))(y_(p_i))^(1/d)=R.   (8)

Every inequality is an equality. By (5), `K_q=L`. The complete joint
equality classification makes all marked input bodies positively
homothetic. Their energies are all `R^d`, and the energy scales by the
`d`th power under homothety, so every homothety factor is one. Thus their
centered bodies are the same body `B`, and `L=y+B`. Uniqueness at the
target gives `y=y_q`, proving (7). Any integer point of `conv(J)` has
such a finite positive-weight representation, proving part 2.

No global affine formula for `p -> y_p` is asserted merely from these
anchored equalities. Unrelated lattice vertices can have no nontrivial
integer anchored relation. The equal-centered-body conclusion propagates
along the hypergraph of actual anchored relations in `J`, and is only
asserted where those relations connect the bases.

## 4. Exact relation to the archived midpoint and forest statements

The archived constant-volume chain statement in `candidate 516ae9c5f80f607b`,
Section 5, starts with equal volumes on an ENTIRE consecutive chain and
uses equality in ordinary Brunn--Minkowski. The present result instead
selects an attained deepest energy stratum in an arbitrary family. Equal
energy concerns marked points and is not assumed to be equal volume;
the equal-volume and equal-shape conclusion is forced on each actual
anchored relation by joint energy equality.

The zero-forest obstruction in
`candidate 588eabf65d9a1440` shows that
equalities on a chosen parity forest do not imply a global centroid-graph
Helly bound. Here (7) holds for EVERY anchored relation within `J`, in
particular every distinct same-parity pair. It says nothing about pairs
in `P` whose endpoints are not both in `J`.

An optional genuine payment follows from the already proved theorem in
`candidate 1b856082117c9e20`, Sections
1--2. Let `M_J=sum_(p in J)|K_p|` and let `k(J)` be its number of occupied
parities. Along every same-parity pair, (7) makes the ordinary centroid
of the midpoint fiber the average of the two endpoint centroids. The
actual restricted family on the complete base `J` therefore has maximum
raw depth at least

    Gamma_d M_J/k(J),                                  (9)

strictly greater if `|J|>k(J)`, by that archived theorem. Original cap
mass dominates restricted cap mass at every point, so the ORIGINAL
maximum `Q` satisfies the same weak or strict bound. The point paying
(9) need not be one of the selected points `(p,y_p)`.

Consequently a hypothetical strict bad family with
`Q<Gamma_d M/k(P)` must satisfy `M_J/M<k(J)/k(P)`. This is a proved
restriction on the selected subfamily, not a proof that it has sufficient
original mass, not an assertion that `J` is all deepest bases, and not
a deformation reducing the original normalized maximum.
